referenceSources.label: RSPB — Robin
referenceSources.verified: Adult orange-red face and breast, brown upperparts; adult male and female have matching appearance.

review.anatomy: Tête frontale complète ; face orange, petite calotte brune, petit bec fermé ; pas de corps ni d’accessoire.
review.thumbnailReview: Orange round face and short bill remain distinct on both backgrounds at 45 px.

referenceSources.label: RSPB — Blue Tit
referenceSources.verified: Blue cap, white face, dark eye stripe, very short thin black beak.

review.anatomy: Tête frontale complète ; calotte bleue, joues blanches et bande oculaire sombre, bec court ; silhouette distincte du rougegorge.
review.thumbnailReview: Blue cap, white cheeks and dark facial band read clearly at 45 px.

referenceSources.label: RSPB — Hoopoe
referenceSources.verified: Pinkish-brown crest, dark downward-curved bill, black and white markings.

review.anatomy: Tête et huppe éventail à pointes noires entières ; bec long fermé jusqu’à sa pointe ; aucune portion de cou ou de corps.
review.thumbnailReview: Complete black-tipped crest and long bill are clear at 45 px.

referenceSources.label: LPO — Cigogne blanche
referenceSources.verified: Adult white head and long red pointed bill; marshes and meadows.

review.anatomy: Frontal white bird head, complete long straight red closed bill, no neck or wings.
review.thumbnailReview: White head and complete red pointed bill are readable on light and dark backgrounds at 45 px.

referenceSources.label: RSPB — Spoonbill
referenceSources.verified: White bird, long broad black spoon-shaped bill; breeding adult has yellow bill tip and short crest.

review.anatomy: White crested head, full black spatulate bill with rounded yellow tip, distinct from stork.
review.thumbnailReview: Distinct broad rounded yellow-tipped paddle bill and white crest visible at 45 px.

referenceSources.label: San Diego Zoo — Saiga
referenceSources.verified: Cinnamon-buff coat, enlarged drooping nose, male ridged amber horns; open steppe.

review.anatomy: Complete pair of ridged horns and ears, enlarged pendulous nose with two nostrils, head only.
review.thumbnailReview: Drooping broad nose, ridged horns and both ears provide distinct silhouette at 45 px.

referenceSources.label: San Diego Zoo — Caracal
referenceSources.verified: Unspotted reddish-gold fur, long black ear tufts; arid savanna and semi-desert.

review.anatomy: Complete long black ear tufts, unspotted tawny coat, vertical cat pupils, white lower muzzle.
review.thumbnailReview: Black ear tufts and large pointed ears remain clear at 45 px; feline silhouette distinct.

referenceSources.label: Chester Zoo — Aardvark
referenceSources.verified: Orycteropus afer; long snout and pointed ears.

referenceSources.label: Michigan State University — Aardvark specimen
referenceSources.verified: Pinkish-grey thick skin with sparse dull brown-grey bristles, long blunt muzzle with round nostrils.

review.anatomy: Complete tall ears, elongated pinkish snout with two nostrils, sparsely bristled brown-grey head.
review.thumbnailReview: Tall ears and pink elongated nostril snout remain visible at 45 px.

referenceSources.label: Zoo de Guadeloupe — South American coati
referenceSources.verified: Red coati species Nasua nasua.

referenceSources.label: Zoo Brasilia — Quati
referenceSources.verified: Nasua nasua, triangular head, small round ears and narrow snout.

referenceSources.label: San Diego Zoo — Coati
referenceSources.verified: Long mobile snout and forest habitats; distinguishes Nasua nasua from white-nosed Nasua narica.

review.anatomy: Small round ears, brown elongated tapered muzzle, reddish coat and restrained pale facial markings; head only.
review.thumbnailReview: Reddish triangular head, small round ears and long dark muzzle read at 45 px.

referenceSources.label: Smithsonian — Nine-banded armadillo
referenceSources.verified: Dasypus novemcinctus; leathery bony plates forming head armor.

referenceSources.label: University of Michigan — Nine-banded armadillo
referenceSources.verified: Partly plated head, hairless long ears, tapered softer pinkish muzzle; nine bands are on back, not head.

review.anatomy: Frontal head with leathery crown plates, unarmored ears, tapered long muzzle; no back bands copied onto face.
review.thumbnailReview: Plate texture across head and triangular long muzzle remain visible at 45 px; distinct from furry mammals.

referenceSources.label: Australian Museum — Greater Bilby
referenceSources.verified: Macrotis lagotis, blue-grey silky fur, very long pinkish ears and pointed snout.

review.anatomy: Complete tall pink ears, blue-grey coat and narrow pointed snout; no rabbit incisors.
review.thumbnailReview: Complete long pink ears and pale grey pointed face remain readable at 45 px. Potential sibling silhouette: aardvark/rabbit.

referenceSources.label: Australian Museum — Southern Cassowary
referenceSources.verified: Casuarius casuarius; large grey-brown helmet and bare blue head skin. Red wattles are on neck and excluded from head-only form.

review.anatomy: Complete single tall casque, blue bare face skin, closed beak, no neck wattles or body.
review.thumbnailReview: Tall complete brown casque and blue face make unmistakable silhouette at 45 px.

referenceSources.label: New Zealand DOC — Kākāpō
referenceSources.verified: Kākāpō, green flightless nocturnal parrot with owl-like facial disc.

referenceSources.label: New Zealand Birds Online / Te Papa, DOC and Birds NZ — Kākāpō
referenceSources.verified: Scientific identity Strigops habroptilus.

review.anatomy: Green mottled crown, pale owl-like facial disc and complete horn-coloured hooked parrot beak.
review.thumbnailReview: Moss-green owl-like disc with pale parrot bill visible at 45 px; distinct from macaws and owls.

referenceSources.label: European Journal of Taxonomy — King cobra revision 2024
referenceSources.verified: Ophiophagus hannah sensu stricto restricted to mainland northern/eastern India, Indo-Burma and Indochina, after four-species revision.

review.anatomy: Complete expanded hood ending without trunk, head crown shields, round pupils and closed mouth, no tongue or fangs.
review.thumbnailReview: Oval expanded hood and pale ventral scale rows visible at 45 px. Hood is the deliberate identifying head-portrait appendage.

referenceSources.label: Zoo Frankfurt — Red-eyed treefrog
referenceSources.verified: Agalychnis callidryas, green coloration and large red eyes.

referenceSources.label: Smithsonian — New red-eyed tree frogs
referenceSources.verified: Natural vivid red eyes and leaf-dwelling treefrog appearance.

review.anatomy: Green complete frog head with vivid red eyes, vertical black pupils and no eyelashes or mammal anatomy.
review.thumbnailReview: Vivid red vertical-pupil eyes against green head remain distinct at 45 px.

referenceSources.label: AMNH — Amphibian Species of the World
referenceSources.verified: Dyscophus antongilii accepted species identity.

referenceSources.label: University of Michigan — Tomato frog
referenceSources.verified: Female bright reddish-orange skin, lower side fading to white and dark stripe behind each eye.

review.anatomy: Orange-red female head, pale lower jaw, golden eyes with horizontal pupils and dark stripes behind eyes.
review.thumbnailReview: Orange-red head and golden horizontal-pupil eyes remain clear at 45 px.

referenceSources.label: Toronto Zoo — Blue poison dart frog
referenceSources.verified: Dendrobates tinctorius azureus, bright blue coloration with irregular dark blue/black head spots.

referenceSources.label: Amphibian and Reptile Conservation — Dendrobates azureus in Suriname
referenceSources.verified: Azureus refers to a population of Dendrobates tinctorius described originally as D. azureus; not counted here as a separate species.

review.anatomy: Blue real azureus form of D. tinctorius, irregular black head spots and dark round-pupil frog eyes; head only.
review.thumbnailReview: Blue head and clear black spots form a distinct silhouette at 45 px; dark frog eyes correctly retained.

referenceSources.label: Université de Bordeaux — Brochet
referenceSources.verified: Esox lucius; elongated freshwater body, depressed elongated snout.

referenceSources.label: DORIS / FFESSM — Brochet
referenceSources.verified: Duckbill-like head, rear dorsal fin, forked tail and long fusiform body.

review.anatomy: Whole elongated pike body, duckbill snout, closed mouth, rear dorsal, paired fins, anal fin and complete forked tail.
review.thumbnailReview: Complete diagonal elongated silhouette, duckbill snout and forked tail remain legible at 45 px.

referenceSources.label: USGS — Wels catfish
referenceSources.verified: Silurus glanis; large scaleless flat head, tiny eyes and exactly six barbels: two long upper, four shorter lower.

referenceSources.label: DORIS / FFESSM — Silure glane
referenceSources.verified: Broad flat head, olive/grey mottled scaleless skin, three pairs of barbels.

review.anatomy: Exactly six complete barbels: two long upper-corner barbels and four short lower-jaw barbels; broad scaleless mottled head, tiny eyes.
review.thumbnailReview: Broad dark head and six separate barbels remain visible at 45 px on both backgrounds.

referenceSources.label: Harvard Museum of Comparative Zoology — Symphysodon discus
referenceSources.verified: Symphysodon discus Heckel, 1840 specimen identity.

referenceSources.label: Farias and Hrbek 2008 — Patterns of diversification in discus
referenceSources.verified: S. discus distinctive broad central black vertical flank band, faint horizontal silvery striations, purplish-grey ground colour.

review.anatomy: Complete circular side-view cichlid body with central broad dark bar, dorsal/anal contour fins, paired fine pelvic rays and full fan tail.
review.thumbnailReview: Round high body, side profile and broad central dark band remain distinct at 45 px.

referenceSources.label: Australian Museum — Yellow Boxfish
referenceSources.verified: Ostracion cubicus; box-shaped body, juvenile bright yellow coloration and pupil-sized black spots.

review.anatomy: Whole angular box-shaped yellow spotted juvenile carapace, paired pectoral fins, dorsal/anal fins and complete tail; no horns.
review.thumbnailReview: Bright yellow compact angular fish body with contrasting black dots remains clear at 45 px.

referenceSources.label: DORIS / FFESSM — Étoile de mer rouge
referenceSources.verified: Echinaster sepositus; red-orange five-armed starfish with irregular small aboral protuberances, hard substrates and seagrass beds.

referenceSources.label: ITIS — Echinaster sepositus
referenceSources.verified: Species Echinaster sepositus, red starfish.

review.anatomy: Exactly five complete gently tapered thick arms, red-orange pebbled dorsal surface, no central face or dorsal mouth.
review.thumbnailReview: Five complete radial red-orange arms make strong distinct silhouette at 45 px, with no invented face.

referenceSources.label: Museums Victoria — Fishes of Australia / Longhorn Cowfish
referenceSources.verified: Lactoria cornuta; long spines project from front head, pale yellow/olive colour and blue spots. Reef-associated sandy/weedy habitats.

review.anatomy: Corrected: exactly two complete long horns, no invented lateral spines, smooth angular side contour, closed tiny fish mouth.
review.thumbnailReview: Exactly two complete long horns, smooth angular head contour and blue spots remain legible at 45 px.

referenceSources.label: NOAA Fisheries — Smalltooth Sawfish
referenceSources.verified: Pristis pectinata is a ray, olive-grey/brown dorsally; long flat rostrum with 22–29 lateral teeth per side. Mouth and gills on underside.

review.anatomy: Complete dorsal three-quarter smalltooth sawfish; 23 distinct lateral rostral teeth on each side (within NOAA 22–29), both broad pectoral fins, pelvic pair, two dorsal fins, full asymmetrical tail, natural dorsal eyes and spiracles, uniform unspotted upper body.
review.toothCountMethod: Visual full-resolution inspection plus independent alpha-contour peak count.
review.thumbnailReview: At actual 45 px on light and dark backgrounds: long straight toothed saw, broad ray fins, and complete tail remain recognizable; no silhouette cropping or background halo.
